title: Rapid purification of gold nanorods for biomedical applications
author: Scaletti, Kim, et al.

steps.title: Synthesize and characterize gold nanorods
steps.instruction: Prepare gold nanorods (GNRs) by a seed‑mediated method based on Nikoobakht et al. and Ratto et al. with slight modifications, yielding rods with aspect ratio 3.9 ± 0.5 (width = 7.5 ± 0.8 nm, length = 28.6 ± 3.5 nm). Characterize the product by transmission electron microscopy on a JEOL 200FX (200 kV tungsten filament) and record optical extinction spectra using a Molecular Devices SpectraMax M2 plate reader.

steps.title: Separate GNRs from excess CTAB
steps.instruction: Transfer the reaction mixture into 2 mL centrifuge tubes and centrifuge with an Eppendorf 5810R at a temperature of 27 °C to remove excess cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and initial by‑products.

steps.title: First centrifugation and resuspend (Sample A)
steps.instruction: Aliquot 1.5 mL of the GNR suspension into each 1.5 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 10 630 rpm (12 000 × g) for 30 min, discard the supernatant leaving ≈50 µL with the pellet, add 1.45 mL Milli‑Q water to resuspend to a final volume of 1.5 mL, and combine all resuspended tubes as Sample A.

substeps.instruction: Place 1.5 mL GNR solution per tube.
Add 1.45 mL Milli‑Q water, mix to 1.5 mL total.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and collect fractions (Samples B & C)
steps.instruction: Take the product from the first centrifugation, distribute 1.5 mL per tube, centrifuge at 6000 rpm (3824 × g) for 15 min, collect the supernatant as Sample B, retain the ~50 µL pellet (spheres and cubes), resuspend the pellet with 1.45 mL Milli‑Q water to 1.5 mL total and combine as Sample C.

substeps.instruction: Place 1.5 mL of the first‑cycle product per tube.
Add 1.45 mL Milli‑Q water, mix to 1.5 mL total → Sample C.

steps.title: Characterize separated nanoparticle fractions
steps.instruction: Observe the distinct colors of Samples A, B, and C, then record optical extinction spectra and acquire TEM images for each sample to assess structural and optical properties.

steps.title: Quantify separation by size and volume
steps.instruction: Measure the dimensions of 300 particles per sample with ImageJ (spherical diameter = 28.6 ± 4.7 nm; cube side = 14.1 ± 2.9 nm; GNR width = 7.5 ± 0.8 nm, length = 28.6 ± 3.5 nm), calculate individual volumes (treat GNRs as a cylinder with two hemispherical caps), and express the results as volume percentages of by‑products versus GNRs: Sample A = 41.5 % by‑products, 58.5 % GNRs; Sample B = 20.6 % by‑products, 79.4 % GNRs; Sample C = 85.8 % by‑products, 14.2 % GNRs.

substeps.instruction: Measure 300 particles per sample using ImageJ.
Record average dimensions for spheres, cubes, and GNRs.
Calculate volume percentages of by‑products and GNRs for each sample.
Report: Sample A = 41.5 % by‑products / 58.5 % GNRs; Sample B = 20.6 % by‑products / 79.4 % GNRs; Sample C = 85.8 % by‑products / 14.2 % GNRs.
